description: Make failures and silence VISIBLE in bot.py so 'no alarm' can never again mean 'silently broken'. Today main() catches every exception, prints to stderr, and exits 2 with no Slack signal; fetch_notices() raises RuntimeError on API drift (HTML instead of JSON); and notify() only sends Slack `if cfg.slack_webhook_url`, so a missing webhook secret is a silent no-op with exit 0. This feature adds: (a) a best-effort Slack failure notification posted when a run fails, (b) an explicit error (not silent skip) when SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL is missing during a real run, and (c) an optional heartbeat mode so the operator gets a periodic 'still alive' signal. All new message-building logic must be pure/testable and covered by offline tests. Depends on FEAT-001 (test scaffold).
steps: Add a pure builder `build_failure_attachments(*, feed_name, error_summary, base_url='')` in bot.py near build_ping_attachments, returning a red color-bar attachment (color '#e01e5a' or similar) with a section block describing the failure and a KST timestamp context block. Keep the error_summary truncated (e.g. first ~500 chars) to avoid huge payloads and never leak secrets (do not echo env values).

Add a function `send_failure_notification(session, *, cfg, error_summary)` that builds the failure attachments and calls send_slack_message with a plain fallback text like '[ERROR] {feed_name} 알림 봇 실행 실패'. It must be best-effort: wrap its own send in try/except and print to stderr on secondary failure so the original error is never masked.

Refactor main() so that when run(cfg) raises OR exits non-zero due to an exception, the bot attempts send_failure_notification before exiting non-zero. Implementation approach: build cfg first (so we know the webhook + feed name), then call run(cfg) inside try/except; on requests.HTTPError / requests.RequestException / RuntimeError / generic Exception, print the existing stderr message AND, if cfg.slack_webhook_url is set and not in dry_run, post the failure notification, then SystemExit(2). Be careful that config-build errors (before cfg exists) still exit non-zero without crashing the notifier itself.

Add a heartbeat mode: a new CLI flag `--heartbeat` (and Config.heartbeat field, wired in parse_args and build_config_from_env_and_args). In run(cfg), handle heartbeat similarly to ping but with a distinct message (e.g. '[HEARTBEAT] {feed_name} 알림 봇 정상 동작 중') using build_ping_attachments or a small dedicated builder. Heartbeat requires SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and does not touch state.

Fix the silent Slack skip: in run(cfg) normal path, BEFORE fetching/notifying, if not cfg.dry_run and not cfg.slack_webhook_url and there is no Notion target configured either, raise a clear error (e.g. `_require(bool(cfg.slack_webhook_url) or (cfg.notion_token and cfg.notion_page_id), 'SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL(또는 Notion 설정)이 없어 알림을 보낼 수 없습니다.')`) so a missing webhook is a visible failure, not exit 0. Keep dry-run working without a webhook.

Ensure fetch_notices' existing RuntimeError on API drift now propagates into the new failure-notification path (it should automatically, since main() will catch RuntimeError). No behavior change needed beyond main() handling it.
Update requirements.txt only if a new runtime dependency is truly needed (it should not be — reuse requests/dotenv).

Add offline tests in tests/ for: build_failure_attachments (returns red attachment with error summary, truncates long summaries, does not include secret-looking values), the heartbeat message builder, and the missing-webhook guard (call run() with a Config that has no webhook/notion and dry_run False and monkeypatch fetch_notices to avoid network, asserting SystemExit/RuntimeError is raised). Use monkeypatch/unittest.mock to stub fetch_notices and send_slack_message so no network is required.
acceptance_criteria: A run that raises inside run() (e.g. fetch_notices raising RuntimeError due to API drift) causes bot.py to attempt a Slack failure notification and still exit non-zero. Verified by a test that monkeypatches fetch_notices to raise and send_slack_message to record calls, then asserts send_slack_message was called with the failure text and the process would exit non-zero.
A normal (non-dry-run) invocation with no SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL and no Notion config raises a clear error / non-zero exit instead of silently returning 0. Verified by test.
`python3 bot.py --heartbeat --dry-run` prints a heartbeat message and returns 0; `--heartbeat` without dry-run requires the webhook. Verified by test.
build_failure_attachments truncates overly long error text and never echoes environment secret values. Verified by test.
All existing FEAT-001 tests still pass; `python3 -m py_compile bot.py` exits 0.
verification: python3 -m pytest tests/ -v  (or `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`) and confirm all tests pass, including the new failure-notification, heartbeat, and missing-webhook-guard tests
python3 bot.py --heartbeat --dry-run  (should print heartbeat text and exit 0 without network)
findings: Implemented in bot.py + tests/test_bot.py only (workflow/README/env.example untouched, left for FEAT-003). Added: (1) build_failure_attachments(*, feed_name, error_summary, base_url='') -> red '#e01e5a' attachment with a section (code-fenced summary) + KST context block; truncates error_summary to MAX_ERROR_SUMMARY_CHARS=500 with '…(생략)' suffix and never receives/echoes secret values. (2) build_heartbeat_attachments (green '#2eb67d', '정상 동작 중'). (3) send_failure_notification(session, *, cfg, error_summary): best-effort, no-op if no webhook, wraps its send in try/except so the original error is never masked. (4) Config.heartbeat field + --heartbeat CLI flag wired through parse_args/build_config_from_env_and_args. (5) run(): heartbeat mode handled like ping with '[HEARTBEAT] {feed_name} 알림 봇 정상 동작 중'; --heartbeat --dry-run prints and returns 0, otherwise _require webhook. (6) Missing-webhook guard: in normal (non-dry-run, non-init) path, _require(webhook OR (notion_token AND notion_page_id)) before fetch, so missing webhook is a visible non-zero failure not a silent exit 0. (7) main() refactor: build cfg first (config-build errors exit 2 safely without touching notifier); run(cfg) wrapped so RuntimeError/HTTPError/RequestException/generic Exception AND non-zero SystemExit from run() trigger _report_failure() (stderr + best-effort Slack failure notification when webhook set and not dry_run) before SystemExit(2); argparse SystemExit (--help/bad args) and rc==0 propagate unchanged. IMPROVEMENT: made the requests.Session lazy inside run() (get_session()) so dry-run paths (ping/heartbeat/init) never build the network stack — this is what lets `--heartbeat --dry-run` return 0 offline. ENV NOTE: sandbox has NO 'requests' installed and only urllib3 1.25.10 (old, lacks Retry(allowed_methods=...)), so `python3 bot.py --heartbeat --dry-run` fails at the top-level `import requests`; verified equivalently via tests/_stubs shim -> prints heartbeat, exit 0. No new third-party imports, so tests/_stubs.py needed no changes; requirements.txt unchanged. Tests: added BuildFailureAttachmentsTests, BuildHeartbeatAttachmentsTests, HeartbeatModeTests, MissingWebhookGuardTests, FailureNotificationTests (14 new; tests patch bot._requests_session, bot.fetch_notices, bot.send_slack_message to stay offline). Verification: `python3 -m py_compile bot.py` exits 0; `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` -> 40 passed (26 existing + 14 new) on host Python 3.9.25.
